subject: Tier portability and fallback playbook for ThriveWell pilot
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@thrivewell.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot packaging question — seat vs throughput fallback

Hi Sergio / Ben,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the team loved the latency profile on the hosted GA model. Before procurement drafts an SOW we need clarity on packaging for the pilot (3-month, 50-seat equivalent) and what Redwood offers if our usage patterns shift mid-pilot. Specifically:

- If we exceed concurrent throughput, can we auto-failover to a higher-throughput tier or does that require a formal amendment?
- What does an in-flight downgrade look like (e.g., seat -> token-metered)? Any prorate rules or credits?
- Are there built-in fallbacks that preserve request reliability (canary to smaller model, region failover, Dedicated burst)?

We'd like a short playbook to present to our procurement and SRE teams. If you can send a one-pager and a sample SLA/redline we can kick off legal.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morris
Head of ML Ops | ThriveWell Labs
elena@thrivewell.com
[attachment: ThriveWell_PO.xlsx (XLSX) referenced for procurement timeline]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena@thrivewell.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — seat vs throughput fallback

Hi Elena — great to hear the demo resonated. Quick answers and a proposed playbook below; attaching a draft SLA with fallback clauses for legal review.

Short answers:
- Auto-failover: We can enable policy-based routing for the pilot. By default, overflow will route to a compatible model variant we host (same family, higher throughput). That change is tracked as a temporary routing override and does not require a contract amendment for the pilot period.
- Downgrade/proration: Downgrades within the pilot window are allowed with prorated credits back to the next billing cycle; we cap concession to protect baseline throughput. Specific numbers in the SLA draft.
- Reliability fallbacks: options include model-variant canary (fastest), region fallback (if the region is enabled), or Dedicated-capacity burst (requires pre-approved burst tokens). We recommend enabling model-variant canaries + a small burst bucket for the pilot.

Proposed 1-page playbook (summary):
1) Normal: 50-seat equivalent quota on hosted GA model.
2) Surge (temporary): auto-route overflow to GA-compact variant for 30 minutes, then escalate if sustained.
3) Sustained overage (>6 hours/day for 3 days): notify and trigger optional Dedicated burst (preapproved tokens).
4) Downgrade path: customer can request seat->metered conversion; credits prorated to next invoice minus a 10% operational reconfiguration fee during pilot.

Next steps:
- I attached ThriveWell_SLA_draft.pdf with the fallback language.
- Ben, can you confirm the maximum pilot concession we can offer (discount or credit) for a 3-month engagement?
- Elena/Kyle, if you want, we can run a 45 minute workshop with SRE + procurement next Tue.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
[attachment: ThriveWell_SLA_draft.pdf (PDF)]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: concession ask for ThriveWell pilot (THRIVE-1629)

Ben / Lauren — looping you in on ThriveWell's pilot. Elena asked for a clear fallback + a small concession to make procurement comfortable. Key ask:
- Pilot length: 3 months, committed 50-seat equivalent.
- Requested concession: 20% off list and a one-time 5k credit if they hit >120% usage in month 2.

My recommendation: approve a limited concession: 12% off list for the pilot + a conditional credit up to $3k (payable after usage threshold confirmed). Keep the SLA draft language we attached; it limits operational exposure by requiring sustained overage before Dedicated burst kicks in.

Why: we get strong upsell signal from their engineering team; flexible routing + canary protects our serving surface. Benchmarks: GA-compact reduces cost ~30% vs GA-standard, which we can route to automatically.

If you approve, I'll send the one-pager and updated SLA to Elena and schedule the SRE workshop.

— Sergio

From: Elena Morris <elena@thrivewell.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Kyle Patel <kyle.patel@thrivewell.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging question — seat vs throughput fallback

Sergio — thanks for the clear breakdown. Workshop next Tue works for our SRE. Procurement is happy to see the prorate rules; they asked for one clarification: can the credit be used to offset Dedicated burst charges or only invoice credits?

Also attaching a quick calendar and PO draft so we can align timing.

Thanks,
Elena
[attachment: ThriveWell_PO.xlsx (XLSX) — draft PO attached]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-16T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: concession ask for ThriveWell pilot (THRIVE-1629)

Approved with guardrails.
- Concession: 12% off list for the 3-month pilot.
- Conditional credit: up to $3,000, payable as invoice credit only (not redeemable for Dedicated burst tokens).
- Operational: require SRE workshop and explicit routing policy in the SLA.

Sergio — send the one-pager + update the SLA to mark the credit as invoice-only. If they sign the PO this week, we can enable the pilot on 2026-09-29.

LaurEN Bishop
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
